builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agents, Think Only When it Helps
summary: The method replaces the common practice of distilling complete teacher trajectories with interleaved thoughts and actions by training only on thoughts whose information is not already disclosed in actions. It reduces supervision and training-data cost when thoughts are redundant, while adding the complexity of identifying discrepant cases where thoughts carry unique information. It can fail if informative reasoning is mistakenly treated as redundant and removed, degrading student performance in cases where actions do not reveal the needed information.
rationale: This can reduce distillation cost for small teams, but the gain depends on correctly detecting when teacher thoughts add information beyond actions, so it should be validated on the reader’s workload before adoption.
technique: Selective thought supervision in agent distillation

claims.statement: The method replaces the common practice of distilling complete teacher trajectories with interleaved thoughts and actions by training only on thoughts whose information is not already disclosed in actions. It reduces supervision and training-data cost when thoughts are redundant, while adding the complexity of identifying discrepant cases where thoughts carry unique information. It can fail if informative reasoning is mistakenly treated as redundant and removed, degrading student performance in cases where actions do not reveal the needed information.

Altering or discarding thought supervision has little effect on student action performance on agent benchmarks across model scales, except when thought information is not disclosed in the corresponding action.
